## 🌎 Geopolitics

### Trump Will Raise Iran, Not Ukraine, in Planned Trilateral with Putin and Xi

President Trump will address Iran during his upcoming meetings with Russian President Putin and Chinese President Xi, but Ukraine will be notably absent from the agenda, a White House official confirmed on November 14, 2026. The trilateral discussion marks Trump's first major diplomatic engagement with both nuclear powers since taking office. No ceasefire or resolution expectations have been set, but the agenda signals a strategic rebalancing toward containment of Iran and management of great-power competition.

**Why it matters.** This pivot away from Ukraine and toward Iran cuts to the core of global stability—and India's position in it. For a consultancy tracking emerging-market energy flows and geopolitical risk, the Iran angle matters enormously: US-Iran escalation could spike oil prices, tighten sanctions enforcement against Russian oil (which India imports heavily), and force New Delhi to choose between Washington's Iran line and its pragmatic energy security. The fact that Ukraine is off the Trump-Putin-Xi table suggests the US is no longer treating European security as central to US-China-Russia diplomacy. India, positioned as a US technology and defense partner but still reliant on Russian energy and neutral on Ukraine, faces a calculus shift: if the US is pivoting to great-power management rather than Ukraine defense, New Delhi's own alignment with the West on tech and defense becomes more conditional.

**Action.** Monitor Trump's China trip itinerary and confirm when the trilateral occurs. Track oil markets and US-Iran rhetoric for shifts in sanctions enforcement or escalation signals. Watch whether Japan, South Korea, or India are consulted beforehand—their exclusion would underscore that Trump sees this as a pure great-power summit, not a coalition builder.

*Sources: [[Times of Israel liveblog, November 14, 2026](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog-november-14-2026/)]([Times of Israel liveblog, November 14, 2026](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog-november-14-2026/)) · [[The Diplomat](https://thediplomat.com/)]([The Diplomat](https://thediplomat.com/))*

### Russia and Ukraine Begin Direct Talks in Abu Dhabi, Zelenskyy Calls First Day "Constructive"

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the first day of US-mediated trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10, 2026 as "constructive and quite substantive"—marking the first direct Russia-Ukraine negotiations since February and the first US-brokered trilateral in nine months. The Russian delegation, led by Vladimir Medinsky, spent nearly four hours with Ukrainian counterparts discussing prisoner exchanges, humanitarian corridors, and European security architecture. Secretary of State Marco Rubio called the session "very productive," though neither side released a joint statement or announced a framework for further negotiations.

**Why it matters.** Ukraine peace talks reshape European security—and India's calculations around it. As a founding member of the Non-Aligned Movement and a voice for the Global South, India has navigated between US backing and Russian pragmatism. If these talks produce a ceasefire or settlement framework, the implications ripple across India's defense procurement (Russia remains a supplier despite Ukraine ties), energy security, and its own US-India defense partnership. A Ukrainian settlement could also free up Western military and financial resources, potentially shifting US focus—and investment—toward Indo-Pacific deterrence of China. For an India-market consultancy, a Ukraine peace would unlock European capital and attention for India's growth story, but it also means a reduced US need for India as a Russia counterweight.

**Action.** Monitor the second day of Abu Dhabi talks (November 11) for outcomes. Read Zelenskyy's full remarks and Medinsky's statements for any disclosed framework on territorial concessions or ceasefire terms. Track how European allies (UK, France, NATO) react—their buy-in will determine whether a deal holds or becomes a US-Russia bilateral that sidelines Ukraine.

*Sources: [[Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/10/russia-ukraine-and-us-to-meet-as-zelenskyy-claims-battlefield-successes)]([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/10/russia-ukraine-and-us-to-meet-as-zelenskyy-claims-battlefield-successes)) · [[NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/10/g-s1-152773/russia-ukraine-war-talks)]([NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/10/g-s1-152773/russia-ukraine-war-talks)) · [[Washington Post](https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2026/11/10/russia-ukraine-begin-us-backed-peace-talks-abu-dhabi/)]([Washington Post](https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2026/11/10/russia-ukraine-begin-us-backed-peace-talks-abu-dhabi/))*

## 🧠 Artificial Intelligence

### Gemini 4 Carbon now available to all users with cybersecurity and extended reasoning focus

Google rolled out Gemini 4 Carbon to general availability on November 10, 2026, after weeks of preview access for security researchers. The frontier model is now available through the Gemini API, Google AI Studio, and for Gemini Ultra subscribers. Google positions Carbon as its strongest model to date, with enhanced performance on long-horizon reasoning tasks and cybersecurity workflows. Pricing starts at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens through November 30, then rises to $4/$20 per million respectively.

**Why it matters.** Carbon represents a meaningful step forward in model capability parity for long-context reasoning and specialized domains like code security analysis. The phased rollout starting with cybersecurity defenders signals Google's strategy to validate frontier capabilities in high-stakes use cases before wider release. For teams building security-focused AI systems or evaluating frontier models for extended reasoning tasks—document analysis, deep code review, multi-step investigation workflows—Carbon is now the direct alternative to Claude and OpenAI's latest. The pricing structure ($2/$10 intro) is aggressively positioned against Claude Opus 5.5 ($15/$75), making it worth benchmarking against your production models before the November 30 rate change.

**Action.** Run a side-by-side latency and accuracy evaluation of Carbon against your current frontier model on a representative subset of your long-horizon or security-focused workloads. Use the introductory pricing window (expires November 30) to measure cost-per-task and throughput with real production queries. If cybersecurity analysis or multi-turn reasoning is a bottleneck in your current pipeline, test Carbon's performance before the price increase. Anthropic's official announcement lacks detail, so verify the context window length and token limits through the Gemini API docs before committing.

### Anthropic ships Claude Fable 5.2 with 20% price cut and 30% speed gain

Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and its restricted counterpart Mythos 5.2 on November 9, 2026. Fable 5.2 is positioned as Claude's most capable flagship model, available to all customers at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens—20% cheaper than Fable 5.1. The company reports 30% faster output generation, a 1M-token context window, and a June 2026 knowledge cutoff. Mythos 5.2 offers the same underlying capabilities for verified organizations with relaxed safety guardrails.

**Why it matters.** The price-performance move is significant for teams running high-volume production inference. A 20% price reduction plus 30% throughput improvement compounds to roughly 50% better cost-per-task efficiency, which reshapes unit economics for any system serving multiple concurrent users or long-running batch jobs. For engineers deciding between Claude and Gemini for production systems, the new Fable pricing ($8/$40) undercuts Claude Opus 5.5 ($15/$75) while claiming to match or exceed its capabilities. The 1M context window remains state-of-the-art for retrieval-augmented and multi-document workflows. Anthropic does not recommend Fable as a starting point; Opus 5.5 is the stated default—this suggests Fable targets high-complexity reasoning over breadth.

**Action.** Migrate any production workloads currently on Fable 5.1 to Fable 5.2 and measure end-to-end latency and cost before and after. For teams evaluating models, benchmark Fable 5.2 against Gemini 4 Carbon on tasks requiring extended reasoning (the 1M context) and long-tail domain knowledge (finance, law, science). Check whether the claimed 30% speed improvement holds under your actual token distribution and request volume. Anthropic's official docs do not yet publish detailed benchmark comparisons; the "#1 on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index" claim is third-party and should be verified against your own tasks.

*Sources: [[Anthropic announcement](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-2)]([Anthropic announcement](https://www.anthropic.com/news/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-2)) · [[9to5Mac technical rundown](https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/09/anthropic-upgrades-claude-with-new-fable-5-2-model-details-here/)]([9to5Mac technical rundown](https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/09/anthropic-upgrades-claude-with-new-fable-5-2-model-details-here/)) · [[TheNewStack coverage](https://thenewstack.io/anthropic-fable-coding-upgrade/)]([TheNewStack coverage](https://thenewstack.io/anthropic-fable-coding-upgrade/))*

## 🇮🇳 India

### Razorpay Clears SEBI's Gate for ₹6,000 Crore IPO, Eyes $5 Billion Listing

Fintech unicorn Razorpay has cleared SEBI's approval for an IPO pegged at ₹5,000–6,000 crore with a mooted $5 billion valuation, according to sources cited by multiple outlets in early November. The fintech enabler's revenue grew 65% in the latest period. SEBI approval paves the way for a Q1 2027 listing; Razorpay had confidentially filed draft IPO papers on June 12, 2026.

**Why it matters.** This is the largest Indian fintech IPO since 2023 and signals that the payments-infrastructure play—not just quick-commerce or SaaS—can now command scale and profitability that merit public markets. For engineers and founders in India's fintech and B2B payments space, Razorpay's IPO runway validates the merchant-stack-as-infrastructure thesis and will likely accelerate IPO pipelines for rivals (Instamojo, Pine Labs, others in the wings). The approval also means payment-rail policy has matured enough that RBI and SEBI can clear a ₹6,000 crore capital raise.

**Action.** Monitor Razorpay's DRHP (Draft Red Herring Prospectus) filing when it goes public; audit their fintech peer list for IPO-readiness signals. Read SEBI's payment-sector guidance updates to understand the regulatory tail winds.

*Sources: [[Inc42](https://inc42.com/buzz/razorpay-gets-sebi-nod-for-₹6000-cr-ipo/)]([Inc42](https://inc42.com/buzz/razorpay-gets-sebi-nod-for-₹6000-cr-ipo/)) · [[YourStory](https://yourstory.com/2026/11/razorpay-gets-sebi-nod-for-rs-5000-6000-cr-ipo-eyes-5b-valuation)]([YourStory](https://yourstory.com/2026/11/razorpay-gets-sebi-nod-for-rs-5000-6000-cr-ipo-eyes-5b-valuation)) · [[Entrepreneur India](https://india.entrepreneur.com/?p=101238)]([Entrepreneur India](https://india.entrepreneur.com/?p=101238))*

### Amazon Backs Greenjoules' ₹150 Crore Series B; TDB Loans ₹100 Crore More for Renewable Fuels

Renewable-fuels startup Greenjoules has secured a ₹150 crore Series B from Amazon's Smbhav Venture Fund and Climate Pledge Fund, of which ₹88 crore is fresh capital (the rest from an August tranche). The Government of India's Technology Development Board (TDB) separately committed a ₹100 crore concessional loan, bringing total secured financing to ₹250 crore. The round was announced November 11, 2026.

**Why it matters.** This is the deeptech playbook crystallizing: a climate-aligned substrate company (renewable biofuels from agri-waste) now has three pillars—Amazon's corporate venture arm, the US Climate Pledge fund, and direct government backing via TDB. For engineers in climate-tech and biotech, it shows that India's government is now willing to back capital-intensive, long-runway plays with concessional debt, not just equity cheques. Amazon's focus here also signals that Smbhav is being redeployed from e-commerce vendor capture into manufacturing and climate—a subtle policy shift toward hard-science startups.

**Action.** File TDB loan terms and track how government capital flows into pre-revenue deeptech (relevant if you're fundraising or advising on grant-backed hardware). Monitor Smbhav's investment thesis by reviewing Amazon's recent Fund expansion announcements for sector hints.

*Sources: [[DealStreetAsia](https://www.dealstreetasia.com/stories/greenjoules-amazon-smbhav-500799/)]([DealStreetAsia](https://www.dealstreetasia.com/stories/greenjoules-amazon-smbhav-500799/)) · [[Inc42](https://inc42.com/buzz/exclusive-greenjoules-raises-₹62-cr-funding-from-amazon-singularity-to-scale-green-energy-operations/)]([Inc42](https://inc42.com/buzz/exclusive-greenjoules-raises-₹62-cr-funding-from-amazon-singularity-to-scale-green-energy-operations/)) · [[StartupFeed](https://startupfeed.in/?p=14262)]([StartupFeed](https://startupfeed.in/?p=14262))*

## 🏗 Tech & Startups

### Marvell-Lumentum $115B Optical Chip Merger Positions Marvell as AI Connectivity Leader

Marvell Technology announced on November 2, 2026, an all-stock acquisition of optical chip maker Lumentum Holdings for approximately $115 billion, making it the largest tech deal of 2026 by equity value. Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 Marvell shares per Lumentum share, valuing each Lumentum share at $1,132. The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2028 after regulatory and shareholder approval.

**Why it matters.** Marvell was built as a fabless semiconductor company selling into storage and cloud networking. This acquisition marks a transformational pivot: adding Lumentum's optical transceivers, lasers, and optical circuit switching moves Marvell from merchant silicon into the physical layer of AI datacenter interconnects—a play on the hypothesis that optical will displace electrical switching as AI models scale beyond current bottlenecks. The deal signals a broader consolidation in AI infrastructure, where chip makers are vertically integrating to capture both layers (compute and connectivity) rather than compete on price alone.

**Action.** Watch regulatory filings for any FTC Hart-Scott-Rodino delays; track Marvell shareholder sentiment and proxy voting—stock initially dropped >10%, a red flag. Read Marvell CEO's acquisition letter and Lumentum's latest investor deck on the optical roadmap. Monitor rival chip makers (Broadcom, Intel) for similar vertical moves into interconnect hardware.

*Sources: [[Marvell to Acquire Lumentum in $115 Billion All-Stock Deal](https://www.techzine.eu/news/infrastructure/145477/marvell-acquires-lumentum-for-115-billion/)]([Marvell to Acquire Lumentum in $115 Billion All-Stock Deal](https://www.techzine.eu/news/infrastructure/145477/marvell-acquires-lumentum-for-115-billion/)) · [[SEC Form 8-K filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001633978/000119312526442758/d163169dex991.htm)]([SEC Form 8-K filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001633978/000119312526442758/d163169dex991.htm)) · [[Lightwave Online: Marvell shores up AI capabilities](https://www.lightwaveonline.com/home/news/55416101/marvell-shores-up-ai-capabilities-with-115b)]([Lightwave Online: Marvell shores up AI capabilities](https://www.lightwaveonline.com/home/news/55416101/marvell-shores-up-ai-capabilities-with-115b))*

### Two Point O Capital Raises $10 Million to Finance Distributed Solar in India

Two Point O Capital, an Indian clean energy financing startup, closed a $10 million Series A led by Transition Venture Capital on November 2, 2026. The company operates a proprietary non-banking financial company (NBFC) arm to underwrite and distribute loans for residential and commercial distributed solar installations. It does not install hardware itself, focusing instead on software-driven loan decisioning and post-deployment asset tracking.

**Why it matters.** Distributed solar financing in India remains fragmented—most homeowners and small businesses pay cash or rely on dealer financing. Two Point O's NBFC-based approach (lending directly to end customers, not dealers) is a playbook that works: it removes dealer margin, improves credit risk measurement via satellite and device telemetry, and scales faster than dealer-dependent channels. The Transition VC backing signals renewed confidence in climate fintech outside the venture-only model, validating the thesis that profitability and growth can coexist in clean energy lending.

**Action.** Track adoption curves on its dashboard (end-customer acquisition cost, asset performance, loan loss ratios). Look for their Series B timing and check whether they expand to battery financing or other renewable energy assets. Monitor competitor funding in the same space—Sunrun, Enphase, and emerging Indian peers like Oorja.

## 🩹 Health & Science

### First functional cure for hepatitis B clears phase 3 with 19% remission rate

GSK and Ionis's bepirovirsen (Hibsago) achieved FDA approval on October 20, 2026, based on two phase 3 trials (B-Well 1 and B-Well 2) in 1,220 adults with chronic HBV on stable nucleotide therapy. Treatment produced functional cure—undetectable HBV DNA and HBsAg for ≥24 weeks post-treatment—in 233 patients (19%) versus none on placebo. Response rates climbed to 26% in the subgroup with baseline HBsAg ≤1,000 IU/mL. A six-month course allows self-administration after the first dose.

**Why it matters.** Chronic hepatitis B infects ~260 million globally and has been a lifelong antiviral suppression paradigm. Bepirovirsen is the first antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapy to offer a path to remission rather than indefinite viral control. This unlocks commercial incentives for curative trials and AI-driven patient stratification on baseline serology—a sharp inflection from the suppress-forever model. Biotech investors will scrutinize durability: whether the 24-week cure window extends and whether responders remain cure-free after 5–10 years post-treatment.

**Action.** Read the B-Well trial results in the New England Journal of Medicine; the NEJM publication contains the per-arm response rates and safety data (including liver inflammation monitored via LFTs). For practitioners, the actionable move is identifying candidates with HBsAg ≤1,000 IU/mL who are nucleot(s)ide-stable—that subgroup's 26% response rate justifies trial use. For AI/health tech builders, this signals demand for serologic biomarker models that predict responders pre-treatment.

*Sources: [[FDA Approves Bepirovirsen for Chronic Hepatitis B](https://www.hcplive.com/view/fda-approves-bepirovirsen-for-chronic-hepatitis-b)]([FDA Approves Bepirovirsen for Chronic Hepatitis B](https://www.hcplive.com/view/fda-approves-bepirovirsen-for-chronic-hepatitis-b)) · [[Breakthrough: FDA Approves First Drug Offering a 'Functional Cure' For Chronic Hepatitis B](https://www.yahoo.com/news/science/articles/breakthrough-fda-approves-first-drug-030000981.html)]([Breakthrough: FDA Approves First Drug Offering a 'Functional Cure' For Chronic Hepatitis B](https://www.yahoo.com/news/science/articles/breakthrough-fda-approves-first-drug-030000981.html)) · [[New England Journal of Medicine — B-Well Trial Publication](https://www.nejm.org)]([New England Journal of Medicine — B-Well Trial Publication](https://www.nejm.org))*

### Danish study of 750,000 pregnancies finds early GLP-1 exposure safe for weight loss

A November 2026 Danish registry analysis of 750,000 pregnancies assessed early exposure to GLP-1 receptor agonists (semaglutide, tirzepatide) in the six months before conception and during early pregnancy. Participants using GLP-1 for weight management showed no increased rates of major pregnancy complications, preterm birth, or birth defects compared to unexposed controls. A separate subgroup of people with diabetes on GLP-1s did show higher preterm birth rates, but researchers attributed this to diabetes as a known pregnancy risk factor, not the drug itself.

**Why it matters.** Millions of reproductive-age people now use GLP-1s for weight loss, and fear of harm has created clinical uncertainty around conception timing. This large-scale human evidence removes one barrier to treatment continuity and clarifies that early accidental exposure during the conception window is not a teratogen. For health-tech builders, it justifies investment in fertility apps and GLP-1 decision-support tools that integrate pregnancy-planning workflows without triggering unnecessary discontinuation. The finding also informs clinical trial design: early exposure windows in observational data now have a precedent.

**Action.** Practitioners should read the registry study (published in Med, November 2026) and the accompanying JAMA Brigham analysis of the "stop or continue" question around pregnancy intention. For patients, the signal is clear: unplanned early exposure is not catastrophic. However, standard medical guidance remains to discontinue GLP-1s before a planned pregnancy, and the diabetes subgroup signal (elevated preterm birth risk) warrants careful counseling for pregnant people with diabetes on these drugs. Builders: consider tiered GLP-1 pregnancy-planning flows that surface reassurance for accidental exposures while enforcing discontinuation for planned conception.

*Sources: [[Study of 750,000 pregnancies reveals a surprising twist about Ozempic and Wegovy](https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261111005911.htm)]([Study of 750,000 pregnancies reveals a surprising twist about Ozempic and Wegovy](https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/11/261111005911.htm)) · [[Study finds no evidence of harm from GLP-1 exposure during pregnancy](https://www.nursingtimes.net/medicine-management/study-finds-no-evidence-of-harm-from-glp-1-exposure-during-pregnancy-29-09-2026/)]([Study finds no evidence of harm from GLP-1 exposure during pregnancy](https://www.nursingtimes.net/medicine-management/study-finds-no-evidence-of-harm-from-glp-1-exposure-during-pregnancy-29-09-2026/)) · [[Study links GLP-1 use to some pregnancy risks — but the research has key caveats](https://www.livescience.com/health/fertility-pregnancy-birth/study-links-glp-1-use-to-some-pregnancy-risks-but-the-study-has-key-caveats)]([Study links GLP-1 use to some pregnancy risks — but the research has key caveats](https://www.livescience.com/health/fertility-pregnancy-birth/study-links-glp-1-use-to-some-pregnancy-risks-but-the-study-has-key-caveats))*

## 🎤 Culture & World

### H.I.G. Forms Waveborn to Consolidate Creator Economy at Scale; Acquires Jake Rosen Entertainment

Private equity firm H.I.G. announced November 13 the formation of Waveborn, a new creator economy platform designed to acquire and scale complementary creator businesses and talent management firms. The company's first acquisition is Jake Rosen Entertainment, a management and production company founded by podcast and content producer Jake Rosen. Waveborn positions itself as infrastructure to aggregate creator IP and talent under institutional capital.

**Why it matters.** This marks a structural shift in how the creator economy is consolidating. Rather than platforms owning creators outright, institutional capital is now buying up the management layer—the firms that negotiate deals, manage talent, and monetize content across platforms. It signals that creator economy IP is mature enough for PE rollup strategies, similar to talent agencies or production companies. For Shashank's audience, this is a distribution insight: the creator economy is moving from platform-native (YouTube/TikTok controlling the relationship) to institutional talent aggregation (PE firms owning the intermediaries).

**Action.** Track whether Waveborn's model scales beyond Jake Rosen (are more acquisitions announced?) and whether other PE firms follow. Watch if traditional talent agencies respond by building creator divisions. The test: does Waveborn create measurable leverage for its acquired creators on platform negotiations, or does it become just another management layer taking percentage cuts?

*Sources: [[H.I.G. Forms Waveborn (PR Newswire)](https://prnewswire.com/news-releases/hig-forms-new-creator-economy-company-waveborn-acquires-jre-302938533.html)]([H.I.G. ### Lionel Messi Wins Back-to-Back MLS Golden Boot, First Player Ever to Achieve it

Lionel Messi won the 2026 MLS Golden Boot on November 8-9 with 26 league goals and 17 assists (43 total goal contributions), becoming the first player in league history to win the award in consecutive seasons. Playing for Inter Miami, he finished ahead of FC Dallas's Petar Musa (22 goals) and Nashville SC's Sam Surridge (21 goals). He had already won the Silver Boot at the 2026 World Cup, where he led Argentina to the final.

**Why it matters.** This is a cultural marker of MLS's shift as a destination for elite talent at their peak. Messi's dominance—winning back-to-back scoring titles—signals that MLS has become a real competitive and cultural draw, not a retirement league. For distribution: MLS media rights (Apple TV+, Univision) are betting on star power to drive viewership, and Messi's sustained excellence validates that strategy. It also reinforces the narrative that the league is becoming a second major destination after Europe, reshaping where global audiences pay attention to soccer.

**Action.** Watch MLS playoffs to see if Messi sustains this form (Inter Miami face Columbus Crew in round one). Track whether his back-to-back Golden Boots translate to MLS media consumption metrics on Apple TV+. Monitor if other elite European players follow Messi's path in the next transfer window—the narrative he creates (MLS as viable destination) can shift the player movement graph.

*Sources: [[ESPN — Lionel Messi MLS Golden Boot 2026 Winner](https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/50411686/lionel-messi-mls-golden-boot-2026-winner-inter-miami)]([ESPN — Lionel Messi MLS Golden Boot 2026 Winner](https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/50411686/lionel-messi-mls-golden-boot-2026-winner-inter-miami)) · [[MLS Soccer Official](https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/inter-miami-s-lionel-messi-wins-2026-mls-golden-boot-presented-by-audi)]([MLS Soccer Official](https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/inter-miami-s-lionel-messi-wins-2026-mls-golden-boot-presented-by-audi)) · [[Al Jazeera — Back-to-back MLS Golden Boot Awards](https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11/8/messi-becomes-first-player-to-win-back-to-back-mls-golden-boot-awards)]([Al Jazeera — Back-to-back MLS Golden Boot Awards](https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11/8/messi-becomes-first-player-to-win-back-to-back-mls-golden-boot-awards))*
